system_overview: This specification models the Non-Blocking Atomic Commitment Protocol (ACP-NB) from Babaoglu and Toueg's work on non-blocking atomic commitment. It extends the simple broadcast variant (ACP-SB) by implementing a reliable broadcast mechanism: when a participant receives a decision, it forwards the decision to all other participants before delivering it locally. This forwarding ensures that even if the coordinator crashes during broadcast, surviving participants can still learn the decision through peer forwarding, guaranteeing termination for all non-faulty participants.
actors_and_components: The system consists of: (1) A single coordinator that collects votes, makes a commit or abort decision, and broadcasts it to participants. (2) A set of participants, each of which votes yes or no, and implements a reliable broadcast by forwarding received decisions to all other participants before finalizing their own decision. Both actors can crash at any time.
state_variables: In addition to all state tracked by the base simple broadcast protocol (participant vote, alive status, decision, faulty flag, vote-sent flag, coordinator request/vote/broadcast/decision/alive/faulty state), each participant also maintains a forwarding table: a mapping from every participant identifier to a forwarding status (not-sent, commit, or abort). This table tracks (a) what pre-decision the participant has received (stored at its own index in the table) and (b) which other participants it has forwarded the pre-decision to.
initial_state: Same as the base simple broadcast protocol, with the addition that all entries in every participant's forwarding table are initialized to not-sent (no decisions received or forwarded yet).
actions: All coordinator actions are inherited from the base protocol (send request, get vote, detect fault, make decision, broadcast, die). The participant actions include the base actions (send vote, abort on vote, abort on timeout for request) plus the following new or modified actions: (1) Pre-decide from coordinator: if a participant is alive and has not yet received a pre-decision, and the coordinator has broadcast a decision to it, the participant stores the decision in its own forwarding entry. (2) Pre-decide from forwarding by another participant: if a participant is alive and has not yet received a pre-decision, and another participant has forwarded a decision to it, the participant stores the decision in its own forwarding entry. (3) Forward: if a participant is alive, has received a pre-decision (its own forwarding entry is set), and has not yet forwarded to another specific participant, it forwards its pre-decision to that participant. (4) Decide (non-blocking): once a participant is alive and has forwarded its pre-decision to all other participants, it finalizes its decision to match its pre-decision. (5) Abort on timeout: if the participant is alive and undecided, the coordinator has died, and no alive participant has received a broadcast from the coordinator, and no dead participant has forwarded a decision to any alive participant, then the participant aborts. (6) Die (crash and become faulty).
safety_properties: AC1 (Agreement): No two participants can reach different decisions -- it is impossible for one to commit while another aborts. AC2 (Commit validity): If any participant commits, then all participants voted yes. AC3 (Abort validity): If any participant aborts, then either some participant voted no, some participant is faulty, or the coordinator is faulty. AC4 (Irrevocability): Once a participant commits or aborts, it remains in that state permanently.
liveness_properties: AC3 liveness: Eventually either all participants reach a decision, or some participant is faulty, or the coordinator is faulty. AC5 (Non-blocking termination): Every non-faulty participant eventually reaches a decision (commit or abort). This property, which the simple broadcast variant does not satisfy, is guaranteed by the reliable broadcast forwarding mechanism.
model_bounds: The set of participants is declared as a constant. For model checking, safety was verified for 4 participants (with symmetries, taking 9 days 14 hours). Liveness was verified for 3 participants.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on participant progress actions (including forwarding and pre-deciding) and coordinator progress actions, excluding death transitions. The reliable broadcast is implemented by requiring participants to forward decisions to all others before finalizing locally. This module extends the base ACP-SB specification and reuses its coordinator logic.
